english_retrieval.snippet: Here’s how a reinvigorated Naveen Patnaik is countering BJP’s rise in Odisha. ## Anti-incumbency, BJP's dominance, and push back after Municipal Election drubbing - challenges were many for Naveen Patnaik. Anti-incumbency, BJP’s dominance, and push back after Municipal Election drubbing – challenges were many for Naveen Patnaik. The by-election, touted to be the semi-finals before Lok Sabha and Assembly election in the state next year, was elevated from a generic by-poll to a battle of prestige. So much so, that Naveen Patnaik had himself campaigned for his party candidate. On the other hand, there was the Bharatiya Janata Party buoyed by its performance in civic body polls which saw a 9-fold increase in the party’s seat share. Remarkably, Congress was seen nowhere in the contest despite the fact that the seat was held by the party for three consecutive terms. Though the contest was a matter of a single assembly seat, it holds higher significance and reflects the efforts being made by Pattnaik to revive his party’s image. The Odisha chief minister re-invented himself with well-planned publicity campaign. Giant billboards sporting Pattnaik’s face with the slogan “Katha nuhen kathina parishram (not words, but hard work)” were seen in the entire state. Despite a reported neck pain, Patnaik travelled through a dozen cities and addressed multiple rallies and gatherings throughout the state. Not only the campaign, Patnaik was also seen making some organisational restructuring. In May, he removed a number of cabinet ministers and directed them to work for strengthening the organisation. In December, the chief minister sacked senior cabinet colleague Damodar Rout for his alleged casteist remarks against Brahmins. And in the latest, Patnaik suspended Baijayant Panda, party’s Lok Sabha MP. Patnaik is also way more active on social media with news and views being pushed out from his twitter handle at a greater pace. The Odisha Chief Minister now has more than two million followers on Twitter. Patnaik was also lauded for his decision to launch a free sanitary napkin scheme for 1.7 million girl students of the state. All in all, Patnaik seems to have taken the challenge of anti-incumbency and heightened efforts from BJP with all seriousness.

Title: Former Odisha minister and veteran BJD leader Damodar Rout passes away | India News - The Indian Express
# Former Odisha minister and veteran BJD leader Damodar Rout passes away. ## Damodar Rout was a seven-time MLA who was actively involved in electoral politics from the 1970s to 2019 and had served in the Cabinet of Naveen Patnaik and his father Biju Patnaik. damodar rout, odisha, indian express. Former Odisha minister and veteran Biju Janata Dal (BJD) leader Damodar Rout passed away early Friday morning while undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Bhubaneswar. Rout, a seven-time MLA, was actively involved in electoral politics from the 70s to 2019 and had served in the Cabinet of Naveen Patnaik and his father Biju Patnaik. Elected to the state Assembly five times from Ersama and twice from Paradeep, both in Jagatsinghpur district, Rout was expelled from BJD in September 2018 for “anti-party” activities. Following his removal from BJD, the veteran leader had joined BJP days before the 2019 polls and also contested the 2019 Assembly elections on a BJP ticket from the Balikuda-Ersama constituency even as the BJD fielded his son Sambit Routray as his replacement from the neighbouring Paradeep constituency. While Rout’s son won the elections, the veteran leader finished third in Balikuda-Ersama, where the BJD candidate won. Months after the 2019 elections, Rout resigned from the BJP alleging he was not being involved in party activities. A veterinary doctor by profession, Rout joined politics in the 70s and considered Biju Patnaik his inspiration. In May 2011, Rout was dropped from the Cabinet for making a casteist slur against some BJD leaders from the Scheduled Caste communities and a senior district official at a meeting in August 2010. Rout had also put the BJD government on the spot for his objectionable remarks against Anganwadi workers and family members of a farmer, who allegedly committed suicide in Bargarh district in November 2017. Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik expressed condolences over Rout’s death. In a post on X, Patnaik said Rout’s demise is an irreparable loss in Odisha politics and his work for the service and development of the people will always be remembered.

HomeFeatures"I forgot my limits": Anurag Kashyap apologises for his alleged casteist remarks... # “I forgot my limits”: Anurag Kashyap apologises for his alleged casteist remarks against Brahmins. Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], April 22 (ANI): Filmmaker Anurag Kashyap apologised for his alleged casteist remarks against Brahmins, saying that he “forgot his limits” while replying to someone in anger. The filmmaker’s post did not go down well, leading to police complaints of allegedly accusing him of hurting the social and religious sentiments of the Brahmins and making objectionable comments against the community. Taking to his Instagram handle, Anurag apologised for speaking badly about the Brahmin community while replying to “someone’s cheap comment” in anger. The filmmaker also admitted that his comments against the Brahmin community disappointed his peers and family. And I spoke badly about the entire Brahmin community. Many intellectuals, whom I respect, are hurt by my anger and my way of speaking,” said Anurag Kashyap. The ‘Gangs of Wasseypur’ director apologised to his colleagues, family and the Brahmin community for his indecent language against the Brahmin caste. I apologise from the bottom of my heart to this community, to whom I did not want to say this, but in anger, I wrote it while replying to someone’s cheap comment. I apologise to all my colleagues, my family and the community for my way of speaking, for my indecent language.”. I hope you will forgive me,” added Anurag Kashyap. > A post shared by Anurag Kashyap (@anuragkashyap10). This is not the first time that the director has issued an apology for his alleged casteist remarks against Brahmins following the controversy. “This is my apology, not for my post, but for that one line taken out of context and the brewing hatred… So, if it’s an apology you’re looking for, then this is my apology,” Kashyap wrote. He also urged the Brahmin community to refrain from targeting his family members and to direct their anger toward him alone. On Saturday, a complaint was lodged in Indore by Anoop Shukla, accusing Kashyap of hurting the social and religious sentiments of the Brahmin community. India needs fair, non-hyphenated and questioning journalism, packed with on-ground reporting.
